issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int for new guest students and a String reason), but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. The template currently only has a TODO for this method. This parameter mismatch will confuse students about the required signature and cause tests (which expect the two-parameter version) to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the solution (and optionally add the correct method stub in the template) to implement the signature specified in the problem: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason). Inside the method, increment numberOfGuestStudents by numberOfNewGuestStudents and (optionally) handle or log the reason parameter. Example: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) { this.numberOfGuestStudents += numberOfNewGuestStudents; /* use reason if needed */ }

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int count and a String reason), but the reference implementation (solution) provides addGuestStudents(int) with only the integer parameter. This signature mismatch (missing String reason parameter) breaks the one-to-one mapping between the specified API and the solution implementation and can confuse students who expect to implement or call addGuestStudents with two parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution's addGuestStudents method to match the specification: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason). Preserve the existing behavior of updating numberOfGuestStudents and either store or log the reason (e.g., add a comment, print it, or add an attribute to keep the last reason) so the method signature matches the problem/UML and students can map the requirement to the implementation.
